title: ShopSphere seeded weaknesses (SIMULATED fixture)
disclaimer: These entries drive the offline mock provider. They are fixtures, not model output. A flaw is only emitted when its applies_when condition matches the current extracted architecture.

security: No threat model or data-flow classification was supplied.
Authentication mechanism for the storefront and admin access is not described.
resilience: Failover test evidence and restore-test results are not provided.
Timeout / retry behaviour for the payment provider call is not described.
finops: No utilisation data or load-test results to justify instance sizing.
No AWS region pricing or commitment information supplied.
compliance: No data-processing inventory or data-classification scheme was supplied.
Data retention schedule for backups is not stated.
performance: No load-test results, connection-pool settings or database IOPS targets were supplied.
operability: No SLO definitions, on-call model or deployment rollback procedure documented.

flaws.title: Orders database endpoint is directly reachable from the internet
flaws.description: {components} is configured with publicly_accessible = true, so the PostgreSQL endpoint receives a public address. Combined with a security group that admits 0.0.0.0/0 on port 5432, the order and customer data store is exposed to the internet rather than only to the application tier.
flaws.scenario: Internet attacker -> scans the public RDS endpoint -> brute-forces or exploits the exposed PostgreSQL service -> reads or tampers with customer and order records.
flaws.impact: Direct compromise path to all order and customer PII; the application tier and WAF are bypassed entirely.
flaws.recommendation: Set publicly_accessible = false, keep the instance in private subnets, and allow port 5432 only from the application security group. Reach the database for administration through a bastion or session manager.
flaws.validation_method: Confirm with `aws rds describe-db-instances` that PubliclyAccessible is false and test connectivity from outside the VPC.
flaws.reasoning: tool SEC-NET-002 reported publicly_accessible = true for the orders database.

rebuttal.argument: The tool observation is a direct read of the declared configuration (publicly_accessible = true) and the database security group admits the whole internet on 5432. Nothing supplied shows a compensating network control such as a VPC-level private endpoint.

flaws.title: Security groups expose database and SSH ports to the whole internet
flaws.description: Security group rules allow ingress from 0.0.0.0/0 to sensitive ports on {components}. This opens PostgreSQL (5432) and SSH (22) to any address, contradicting the stated model of private application instances reached only through the load balancer.
flaws.scenario: Internet attacker -> password-spray or exploit on SSH/PostgreSQL -> shell or SQL access to production hosts -> lateral movement inside the VPC.
flaws.impact: Unrestricted attack surface on administrative and data-plane services; high likelihood of opportunistic compromise.
flaws.recommendation: Remove 0.0.0.0/0 ingress for ports 22 and 5432. Allow 5432 only from the application security group and replace SSH with AWS Systems Manager Session Manager or a restricted bastion.
flaws.validation_method: Review effective security group rules and run an external port scan of the elastic IPs.
flaws.reasoning: tool SEC-NET-001 flagged world-open ingress on security groups app and db.

rebuttal.argument: The cited rules are explicit ingress blocks with cidr_blocks = [0.0.0.0/0] on ports 22 and 5432. Operational convenience does not change the exposure; a time-bound, IP-restricted rule or Session Manager provides the same access safely.

flaws.title: Application role grants all actions on all resources
flaws.description: The inline policy attached to the application role ({components}) allows Action "*" on Resource "*". Any compromise of an application instance yields full administrative control of the AWS account.
flaws.scenario: Attacker exploits a vulnerability in the Java storefront -> reads instance role credentials from metadata -> uses the wildcard policy to create IAM users, read every bucket and delete backups.
flaws.impact: Maximum blast radius: account-wide takeover from a single application-tier foothold.
flaws.recommendation: Replace the wildcard statement with least-privilege actions scoped to the orders queue, specific S3 buckets and CloudWatch logging. Enforce IMDSv2 and consider permission boundaries.
flaws.validation_method: Run IAM Access Analyzer policy validation and review CloudTrail for the actions actually used.
flaws.reasoning: tool SEC-IAM-001 parsed the inline policy statements and found Allow * on *.

rebuttal.argument: The wildcard statement is confirmed, but exploitation requires first compromising an application instance behind the ALB, so likelihood is lower than for an internet-exposed datastore. Severity is adjusted but the least-privilege gap remains.

flaws.title: Database master password is hard-coded in infrastructure code
flaws.description: {components} defines its master password as a literal value in the Terraform source (value redacted by the tool). Anyone with repository or state access can read the production credential.
flaws.scenario: Developer or CI log leaks the repository -> attacker reads the literal password -> authenticates to the production database (especially combined with public exposure).
flaws.impact: Credential disclosure through source control, state files and build logs; no rotation path.
flaws.recommendation: Remove the literal, generate the credential at deploy time (random_password or Secrets Manager), enable managed master user password rotation, and rotate the exposed value immediately.
flaws.validation_method: Search the repository history for the literal and verify rotation in Secrets Manager.
flaws.reasoning: tool SEC-SEC-001 found a literal string for the password attribute.

rebuttal.argument: A literal value for the password attribute is present in the Terraform resource, as recorded by the secret-literal check. Even if it is a placeholder it must not live in code, and Terraform state will store it in clear text.

flaws.title: Media bucket uses a public-read ACL
flaws.description: {components} sets acl = public-read, making every object world-readable and bypassing CloudFront origin controls. Any accidental upload of non-public content becomes immediately public.
flaws.scenario: Developer uploads a customer export or private asset to the media bucket -> object is world-readable -> scraped by search engines or attackers.
flaws.impact: Uncontrolled disclosure of stored objects and loss of the ability to audit or revoke access centrally.
flaws.recommendation: Set the bucket private, enable S3 Block Public Access, and serve public assets through CloudFront with origin access control.
flaws.validation_method: Use S3 Access Analyzer and check the bucket public access block configuration.
flaws.reasoning: tool SEC-STO-001 reported a public ACL.

rebuttal.argument: The ACL is explicitly public-read in the resource definition. Public static content does not require a public bucket: a CDN with origin access control satisfies the same need with auditable access.

flaws.title: Load balancer accepts plaintext HTTP without redirecting to HTTPS
flaws.description: The listener {components} serves HTTP on port 80 and forwards requests to the target group without a redirect action. The document states that TLS terminates at the load balancer, but no HTTPS listener or redirect is defined in the infrastructure.
flaws.scenario: User on an untrusted network follows an http:// link -> session cookie and form data travel in cleartext -> network attacker hijacks the session.
flaws.impact: Exposure of credentials and session tokens; weakens the stated TLS posture.
flaws.recommendation: Add an HTTPS (443) listener with an ACM certificate and convert the port 80 listener to a permanent redirect; enable HSTS in the application.
flaws.validation_method: Request http://<alb-dns> and verify a 301 redirect to HTTPS.
flaws.reasoning: tool SEC-ENC-002 saw an HTTP listener with a forward action only.

rebuttal.argument: The listener on 80 is real and unredirected, but the customer-facing site is reached over HTTPS per the architecture document, so cleartext exposure is limited to users who start from an http:// URL. Severity is reduced; adding the redirect is still recommended.

flaws.title: Orders database storage is not encrypted at rest
flaws.description: {components} explicitly sets storage_encrypted = false. Snapshots and underlying storage hold customer PII in clear form.
flaws.scenario: Snapshot is shared or copied by mistake, or storage media is accessed outside AWS controls -> plaintext PII is readable.
flaws.impact: Weakened confidentiality for stored personal data and backups; fails organisational encryption baseline.
flaws.recommendation: Create an encrypted copy of the instance using a KMS key (snapshot-restore), switch the application over, and enforce encryption with an SCP or AWS Config rule.
flaws.validation_method: Check StorageEncrypted in describe-db-instances output.
flaws.reasoning: tool SEC-ENC-001 saw storage_encrypted = false.

rebuttal.argument: storage_encrypted = false is explicit in the resource. In-place encryption is not possible; remediation requires a snapshot copy with a KMS key, so the finding remains valid until that is done.

flaws.title: Personal-data store lacks encryption at rest (possible control gap)
flaws.description: {components} stores customer personal data (tagged customer-pii) without encryption at rest. Relative to GDPR Art.32 and ISO 27001 A.8.24 this is a possible control gap for protecting personal data; it is an architectural observation, not a legal determination.
flaws.scenario: Backup or snapshot leakage exposes unencrypted personal data, triggering notification obligations assessments.
flaws.impact: Increased likelihood and severity of a personal-data breach if storage is accessed outside normal controls.
flaws.recommendation: Encrypt data stores holding personal data with managed keys and document the key-management approach in the processing records.
flaws.validation_method: Evidence of encryption configuration and key policy for all personal-data stores.
flaws.reasoning: tool SEC-ENC-001 plus the customer-pii tag on the orders database.

rebuttal.argument: The tag customer-pii and the explicit storage_encrypted = false together indicate unencrypted personal data. Provide encryption evidence or a compensating control to withdraw.

flaws.title: Personal-data store is internet-reachable (possible control gap)
flaws.description: {components} holds customer personal data and is publicly accessible. Relative to GDPR Art.25 and Art.32 and ISO 27001 A.8.20 this is a possible control gap in data protection by design; the architecture exposes personal data stores beyond the application tier.
flaws.scenario: Unauthorised access to the public endpoint results in disclosure of personal data to third parties.
flaws.impact: Potentially reportable personal-data breach scenario and loss of accountability over access paths.
flaws.recommendation: Restrict the datastore to private networking and document access paths in the processing inventory.
flaws.validation_method: Network reachability test and architecture review of data access paths.
flaws.reasoning: tool SEC-NET-002 on a store tagged as personal data.

rebuttal.argument: Public accessibility of a personal-data store is a configuration fact. Whatever access controls exist at the database layer, the architecture still exposes the service endpoint beyond the intended trust boundary.

flaws.title: No audit-trail or network flow logging is shown (possible control gap)
flaws.description: The supplied infrastructure contains no CloudTrail trail or VPC flow log resources. Audit logging may be enabled organisation-wide outside this code, so this needs validation. Relative to ISO 27001 A.8.15 it is a possible control gap if absent.
flaws.scenario: Security incident occurs and there is no record of who accessed personal data or how traffic flowed.
flaws.impact: Reduced ability to detect, investigate and evidence access to personal data.
flaws.recommendation: Confirm a multi-region trail and flow logs exist at the account level, or define them in this stack with retention per policy.
flaws.validation_method: Check CloudTrail and VPC flow-log configuration in the target account.
flaws.reasoning: tool COMP-LOG-001 found no audit-trail resources; documentation is silent.

rebuttal.argument: No trail or flow-log resource is defined in the supplied files; please provide evidence of account-level logging.
rebuttal.concede_argument: An organisation-wide trail satisfies the audit-logging concern; withdrawing.

flaws.title: Invoice store has no enforced retention or deletion mechanism (possible control gap)
flaws.description: {components} is tagged as customer personal data and the requirements state a 7-year retention period, but no lifecycle or retention configuration enforces retention or later deletion. Relative to GDPR Art.5(1)(e) storage limitation this is a possible control gap.
flaws.scenario: Invoices are retained beyond the lawful period or deleted too early because retention depends on manual action.
flaws.impact: Storage-limitation and erasure-request obligations cannot be demonstrated technically.
flaws.recommendation: Define S3 lifecycle rules (and object lock if required) matching the 7-year schedule, with expiry and deletion handling for erasure requests.
flaws.validation_method: Review bucket lifecycle configuration and the documented retention schedule.
flaws.reasoning: tool COMP-DATA-001 found a personal-data bucket with no lifecycle configuration while the requirements state 7-year retention.

rebuttal.argument: A stated retention period needs a technical enforcement mechanism; none is declared on the invoices bucket.

flaws.title: Primary orders database runs in a single availability zone
flaws.description: {components} sets multi_az = false. The requirements demand survival of an AZ loss with RPO 5 minutes and RTO 30 minutes and 99.95% availability, which a single-AZ instance cannot meet; an AZ outage or maintenance event takes order processing offline until manual recovery.
flaws.scenario: AZ or instance failure -> database unavailable -> checkout and fulfilment stop until a restore from backup completes (RTO unbounded when backups are disabled).
flaws.impact: Stated availability and RTO/RPO objectives cannot be met; the pilot already saw a 25-minute outage.
flaws.recommendation: Enable Multi-AZ for the RDS instance (or Aurora with replicas in two AZs) and test failover as part of release readiness.
flaws.validation_method: Confirm MultiAZ in describe-db-instances and run a forced failover test.
flaws.reasoning: tool RES-HA-001 saw multi_az = false; CFG-NFR-001 links it to the availability requirement.

rebuttal.argument: multi_az = false is explicit and contradicts the written 99.95% / RPO 5 minute requirement; the incident notes confirm real downtime from a single-instance database.

flaws.title: Automated database backups are disabled
flaws.description: {components} sets backup_retention_period = 0 and skip_final_snapshot = true. Point-in-time recovery is unavailable, so the stated RPO of 5 minutes cannot be achieved and a destructive event is unrecoverable.
flaws.scenario: Operator error or corruption deletes order data -> no automated backup or PITR exists -> permanent loss of orders.
flaws.impact: Unrecoverable data loss; RPO/RTO objectives unattainable.
flaws.recommendation: Set backup_retention_period to at least 7 days, enable PITR, set skip_final_snapshot = false, and schedule a quarterly restore test.
flaws.validation_method: Confirm BackupRetentionPeriod and perform a timed restore test.
flaws.reasoning: tool RES-BAK-001 saw backup_retention_period = 0.

rebuttal.argument: A zero retention period disables automated backups. No alternative backup mechanism is described in the supplied material.

flaws.title: Application tier is confined to one subnet / availability zone with a single instance minimum
flaws.description: {components} places the Auto Scaling group in a single private subnet and permits min_size = 1 with desired_capacity = 1. An instance or AZ failure removes the storefront until replacement completes.
flaws.scenario: Instance health failure or AZ outage -> only instance disappears -> ALB has no healthy targets -> storefront returns 503.
flaws.impact: Application availability is bounded by a single instance and zone, below the 99.95% objective.
flaws.recommendation: Span at least two private subnets in different AZs, set min_size >= 2, and size the pool so the loss of one AZ is tolerated.
flaws.validation_method: Terminate an instance and block an AZ in a game day; verify capacity is retained.
flaws.reasoning: tool RES-HA-004 found min_size = 1 and a single subnet.

rebuttal.argument: vpc_zone_identifier contains one subnet and min_size is 1; both are explicit and prevent tolerance of an AZ loss.

flaws.title: Orders queue has no dead-letter queue
flaws.description: {components} defines no redrive policy. A malformed message is retried until retention expires, blocking consumers and eventually losing orders - exactly the failure seen in the pilot.
flaws.scenario: Poison message crashes the fulfilment worker -> message redelivered repeatedly -> processing stalls -> messages expire after retention and orders are lost.
flaws.impact: Silent order loss and queue stalls; recovery requires manual re-creation of orders.
flaws.recommendation: Create a dead-letter queue, set a redrive policy with maxReceiveCount, alarm on DLQ depth and make the worker idempotent.
flaws.validation_method: Inject a malformed message in staging and verify it lands in the DLQ and raises an alarm.
flaws.reasoning: tool RES-MSG-001 saw no redrive_policy on the orders queue; incident notes describe the same failure mode.

rebuttal.argument: No redrive policy is configured and the pilot incident shows the failure is real, not theoretical.

flaws.title: A single NAT gateway serves all private subnets
flaws.description: Only one NAT gateway ({components}) exists while private subnets span two availability zones. An outage in the NAT's AZ removes outbound access (payment provider calls, patch downloads) for the whole platform.
flaws.scenario: AZ hosting the NAT gateway fails -> instances in the other AZ lose outbound connectivity -> checkout payment calls fail.
flaws.impact: Cross-AZ dependency undermines zone-level redundancy and can break checkout.
flaws.recommendation: Deploy one NAT gateway per AZ with per-AZ route tables, or use VPC endpoints and a regional NAT design.
flaws.validation_method: Review route tables per private subnet and simulate loss of the NAT's AZ.
flaws.reasoning: tool RES-NAT-001: one NAT gateway, subnets in two zones.

rebuttal.argument: One NAT gateway for subnets in two AZs is a structural single point of failure; per-AZ NAT is the standard remedy.

flaws.title: Synchronous payment provider dependency has no documented timeout or fallback
flaws.description: Checkout calls the external Payment Provider API synchronously. The material does not describe timeouts, retries, circuit breaking or a degraded mode, so the behaviour during a provider outage is unknown.
flaws.scenario: Payment provider latency or outage -> checkout threads block -> application pool exhausted -> storefront unavailable.
flaws.impact: Failure of a third party could cascade into full storefront unavailability.
flaws.recommendation: Define client timeouts, bounded retries with jitter, a circuit breaker and a user-facing degradation path (for example deferred capture).
flaws.validation_method: Review client configuration and fault-inject provider latency in staging.
flaws.reasoning: documentation is silent on failure handling for the synchronous external call; absence of evidence, not confirmed absence.

rebuttal.argument: No timeout or circuit-breaker settings were supplied. Provide the client configuration to resolve this.
rebuttal.concede_argument: The described client configuration covers timeouts and circuit breaking; withdrawing this concern.

flaws.title: Very large database instance class selected without sizing evidence
flaws.description: {components} uses a db.r5.4xlarge class with 500 GB storage. No load test or utilisation data was supplied to justify this capacity for a platform expecting roughly 1,500 requests per second at peak. Cost risk is potentially high; actual spend cannot be estimated from the material.
flaws.scenario: Instance runs largely idle outside campaigns while billed continuously (and doubled once Multi-AZ is enabled).
flaws.impact: Potentially significant recurring cost; the magnitude is unknown without utilisation data.
flaws.recommendation: Right-size from load-test results, start smaller with headroom, and evaluate reserved capacity only after stable utilisation data exists.
flaws.validation_method: To estimate actual spend we need: peak/average CPU and memory, IOPS, storage growth, region pricing and commitment options.
flaws.reasoning: tool COST-SIZE-001 flagged a 4xlarge class; no utilisation evidence is available.

rebuttal.argument: No sizing evidence was supplied. Provide load-test or utilisation data supporting the instance class to withdraw this concern.
rebuttal.concede_argument: The described load-test evidence supports the instance class; withdrawing the right-sizing concern.

flaws.title: S3 traffic likely routes through the NAT gateway
flaws.description: A NAT gateway and S3 buckets exist but no S3 gateway VPC endpoint is defined, so private-subnet S3 traffic would incur NAT data-processing charges that a free gateway endpoint avoids.
flaws.scenario: Invoice and media traffic scales with orders and is billed per GB through the NAT gateway.
flaws.impact: Avoidable data-processing cost growing with traffic.
flaws.recommendation: Add an S3 gateway endpoint to the private route tables.
flaws.validation_method: To estimate spend we need monthly S3 transfer volume from private subnets.
flaws.reasoning: tool COST-NAT-001: NAT present, no S3 endpoint.

rebuttal.argument: No VPC endpoint is declared in the supplied infrastructure.
rebuttal.concede_argument: A gateway endpoint exists outside the supplied files, which removes the NAT cost driver; withdrawing.

flaws.title: Logs and objects are retained indefinitely
flaws.description: The application log group has no retention period and the S3 buckets define no lifecycle rules ({components}). Storage cost grows without bound and no tiering applies.
flaws.scenario: Years of logs and objects accumulate in the most expensive storage class.
flaws.impact: Unbounded storage cost growth; also conflicts with data-minimisation practice.
flaws.recommendation: Set log retention (for example 30 days online) and S3 lifecycle rules for tiering and expiry aligned to the retention schedule.
flaws.validation_method: To estimate spend we need log volume per day and object growth rate.
flaws.reasoning: tools COST-LOG-001 and COST-S3-001.

rebuttal.argument: Neither retention nor lifecycle settings are declared; defaults are 'never expire'.

flaws.title: Billable resources carry no cost-allocation tags
flaws.description: Most taggable resources have no tags, so spend cannot be attributed to the storefront, environment or owner.
flaws.scenario: Finance cannot attribute cost growth to services; budgets and anomaly alerts lack dimensions.
flaws.impact: Weak cost visibility and accountability.
flaws.recommendation: Apply mandatory owner, environment and cost-center tags via provider default_tags and enforce with policy.
flaws.validation_method: Run a tag-compliance report and activate cost-allocation tags.
flaws.reasoning: tool COST-TAG-001.

rebuttal.argument: The tag check inspected the declared resources and found most without tags.

flaws.title: Cross-region or replica data movement adds transfer and duplicate storage cost
flaws.description: Replication to a second bucket/region has been introduced ({components}). Inter-region transfer and duplicate storage will add recurring cost; the justification and volume are not stated.
flaws.scenario: Replication traffic grows with invoice volume and is billed per GB plus duplicate storage.
flaws.impact: Additional recurring cost with unknown magnitude.
flaws.recommendation: Document the DR justification (RPO/RTO) and estimate transfer volume; use lifecycle rules on the replica.
flaws.principle: Cost is a design constraint (general practice)
flaws.validation_method: To estimate spend we need replicated volume per month, destination region and storage class.
flaws.reasoning: tool COST-XFER-001 found replication configuration.

rebuttal.argument: Replication is explicit in the revision; cost impact remains unquantified.

flaws.title: Checkout path chains several synchronous hops including an external provider
flaws.description: The request path crosses {components}. With a synchronous external payment call at the end of the chain, a p95 latency target of 300 ms depends on third-party performance that is not budgeted. No load-test data supports the target.
flaws.scenario: Provider latency increases at peak -> request threads wait -> queueing at the application tier inflates p95 beyond 300 ms.
flaws.impact: Latency objective likely violated during peak; cascading slowdown across tiers.
flaws.recommendation: Allocate a latency budget per hop, set aggressive timeouts, and consider asynchronous capture/confirmation for non-critical payment steps.
flaws.validation_method: Load test at 1,500 rps with injected provider latency and measure p95 per hop. Missing: current latency measurements.
flaws.reasoning: tool PERF-CHAIN-001 measured chain length from the extracted relationships.

rebuttal.argument: The extracted dependency chain shows the synchronous external call on the critical path; no latency budget is documented.

flaws.title: Single database instance is shared by storefront and fulfilment workloads
flaws.description: {components} serves both interactive checkout traffic and the fulfilment worker, with no read replicas or cache described. Contention between OLTP and batch-like fulfilment work is plausible at 1,500 rps peak; the saturation point is unknown.
flaws.scenario: Campaign peak -> fulfilment backlog drains concurrently with checkout writes -> lock and I/O contention raise checkout latency.
flaws.impact: Coupled scaling and unpredictable latency under peak load.
flaws.recommendation: Document connection-pool sizing, introduce read replicas or caching for read-heavy paths, and isolate fulfilment access patterns.
flaws.validation_method: Load test mixed workloads; observe connection count, lock waits and IOPS. Missing: peak read/write ratio.
flaws.reasoning: tool PERF-DB-001: multiple consumers of one database.

rebuttal.argument: Two independent consumers share the database per the diagram; capacity under mixed load is unvalidated.

flaws.title: No caching layer is modelled for read-heavy catalogue and session data
flaws.description: The extracted model has no cache or CDN components even though a catalogue and media are served at 1,500 rps peak. A cache may exist but is not described, so this needs validation.
flaws.scenario: Every catalogue read reaches the database or S3, amplifying load during campaigns.
flaws.impact: Higher database load and latency than necessary at peak.
flaws.recommendation: Document or introduce a cache/CDN strategy with invalidation rules for catalogue and media content.
flaws.validation_method: Check cache hit-rate expectations; load-test with and without caching. Missing: read/write ratio.
flaws.reasoning: tool PERF-CACHE-001: no cache/CDN in the model; documentation is silent.

rebuttal.argument: No cache is described anywhere in the supplied material.
rebuttal.concede_argument: The described CDN/cache covers the read-heavy paths; withdrawing the concern.

flaws.moderator_note: The claimed saturation figure cites no measurement or tool observation; marked as requiring validation.
flaws.title: Database will saturate at about 200 requests per second
flaws.description: The database instance will become I/O bound at roughly 200 requests per second, far below the stated peak of 1,500 requests per second.
flaws.scenario: Traffic ramps during a campaign and the database becomes the hard bottleneck.
flaws.impact: Peak traffic cannot be served.
flaws.recommendation: Provision more IOPS or add read replicas.
flaws.validation_method: Run a load test to find the real saturation point.
flaws.reasoning: SEEDED UNSUPPORTED CLAIM - asserts a measurement with no evidence, to exercise moderator validation.

rebuttal.concede_argument: The saturation figure was not derived from supplied measurements; withdrawing.
rebuttal.argument: The figure was not derived from data.

flaws.title: No alarms or notification routing are defined for the platform
flaws.description: The infrastructure defines no CloudWatch alarms or SNS topics. The pilot incident was discovered through a customer ticket rather than monitoring. Alerting may be defined outside this code, so this needs validation.
flaws.scenario: Queue depth or error rate rises overnight with no page -> orders delayed until customers complain.
flaws.impact: Long detection time for outages and silent failures.
flaws.recommendation: Define SLIs/SLOs and alarms (queue depth, 5xx rate, DB CPU/connections, DLQ depth) routed to an on-call rotation.
flaws.validation_method: Review the monitoring account/configuration and alert routing evidence.
flaws.reasoning: tool OPS-ALARM-001 found no alarm resources; incident notes describe late detection.

rebuttal.argument: No alerting resource is declared and the incident notes show detection came from a customer.
rebuttal.concede_argument: Alerting defined in the external monitoring platform addresses the concern; withdrawing.

flaws.title: No dead-letter handling or recovery runbook for asynchronous order processing
flaws.description: Order events flow through {components} with no dead-letter destination, no alarm and no documented failure-recovery procedure ('No formal runbook for queue failures exists yet'). Operators have no defined way to inspect, replay or discard failed messages.
flaws.scenario: Worker crashes on a malformed event -> operators have no DLQ or runbook -> manual, error-prone re-creation of orders.
flaws.impact: Slow, error-prone recovery and repeat of the pilot incident.
flaws.recommendation: Add a DLQ with redrive tooling, a documented replay/discard runbook and an alarm on DLQ depth; assign an owner.
flaws.validation_method: Tabletop the failure scenario with the on-call team and verify the runbook.
flaws.reasoning: tool RES-MSG-001 confirms no redrive; the architecture document states no runbook exists.

rebuttal.argument: The architecture document itself states that no runbook exists for queue failures, and the queue has no redrive policy.

flaws.title: Request-level and log retention settings limit troubleshooting
flaws.description: The load balancer does not enable access logs and the application log group has no explicit retention policy ({components}). Forensics and capacity analysis would lack consistent request-level data.
flaws.scenario: Intermittent 5xx errors cannot be correlated to requests because ALB logs are unavailable.
flaws.impact: Slower root-cause analysis.
flaws.recommendation: Enable ALB access logs to a protected bucket and define retention for the application log group.
flaws.validation_method: Check access_logs.enabled on the load balancer.
flaws.reasoning: tools OPS-LOG-001 and COST-LOG-001.

rebuttal.argument: access_logs is not enabled in the load balancer definition.

flaws.title: Instance-replacement deployments with a single instance imply downtime and no rollback path
flaws.description: Deployments replace instances in the Auto Scaling group, but the group runs a single instance. No rolling/blue-green strategy, health-gated rollout or rollback procedure is documented, so each release is likely to cause downtime.
flaws.scenario: Release replaces the only instance -> storefront unavailable until the new instance passes health checks -> failed release has no automated rollback.
flaws.impact: Release-related outages and slow recovery from bad deployments.
flaws.recommendation: Adopt rolling or blue/green deployment with min healthy capacity, health-gated rollout and automated rollback; document the procedure.
flaws.validation_method: Review the deployment pipeline and perform a rollback drill.
flaws.reasoning: document states instance replacement; ASG min_size = 1.

rebuttal.argument: The document describes replace-in-place deployments and the group has min_size 1; no rollback procedure is supplied.

flaws.moderator_note: The cited Kubernetes pods do not exist in the architecture model; claim is unsupported.
flaws.title: Order pods lack readiness probes
flaws.description: The order service pods in the Kubernetes cluster define no readiness probes, so unready pods receive traffic.
flaws.scenario: Pod restarts receive traffic before ready, returning errors.
flaws.impact: Error spikes during rollouts.
flaws.recommendation: Add readiness and liveness probes to the order pods.
flaws.validation_method: Inspect pod specs.
flaws.reasoning: SEEDED HALLUCINATION - refers to Kubernetes pods that do not exist in this architecture, to exercise moderator rejection.

rebuttal.concede_argument: There are no Kubernetes workloads in this architecture; the finding was in error.
rebuttal.argument: No Kubernetes workloads exist.
